guide.title: How Ohaeng Works
guide.subtitle: A quick primer if saju is new to you — no prior knowledge required.
guide.sajuHeading: Saju vs. horoscope: what's the difference?
guide.sajuBody1: Western astrology reads the sky — where the sun, moon, and planets sat the moment you were born. Saju (사주, "four pillars") reads the calendar instead. Your birth year, month, day, and hour each get translated into a code from an ancient Chinese and Korean dating system — one built from ten "Heavenly Stems" and twelve "Earthly Branches" cycling together, the same system that names lunar years after animals like the Tiger or the Dragon.
guide.sajuBody2: Stack all four — year, month, day, hour — and you get your "eight characters" (팔자), the full saju chart. It's not more or less legitimate than a sun sign; it's just a different, much older tradition that hasn't had its Co-Star moment in the West yet. Ohaeng is our attempt at that.
guide.elementsBody: Every character in your chart maps to one of five elements — Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, Water — and whichever shows up most is your dominant element. The elements aren't just labels; they interact. Each one generates the next (Wood feeds Fire, Fire leaves behind Earth, Earth yields Metal, Metal collects Water, Water nourishes Wood) and overcomes another (Wood parts Earth, Earth dams Water, Water douses Fire, Fire melts Metal, Metal chops Wood). That generating-and-overcoming cycle is the actual engine behind your daily fortune and your idol compatibility results — not a coin flip.
guide.accuracyHeading: This isn't a random number generator
guide.accuracyBody: A lot of horoscope-style apps quietly pick a result at random and dress it up as personal. Ohaeng doesn't — it runs your birthdate through lunar-javascript, an open-source calendar engine built on real historical solar-term and sexagenary-cycle data, the same math traditional manseryeok almanacs use. Two people with the same birthday will always get the same chart, and today's fortune is always the actual Five Element relationship between your chart and today's, not noise.
guide.scoreBody: Every score you see — in Compatibility, Idol Match, Drama Match, or Group Match — comes from the same Five Element relationship described above, turned into a number. Same-element pairs start in the low-to-mid 90s, generating relationships (someone feeding your energy, or you feeding theirs) land in the 70s-80s, and overcoming relationships — the tense, push-and-pull kind — sit lower, in the 40s-60s. Every pair also gets a small individual nudge so two pairings with the same relationship type don't come out looking identical. It's not a random roll layered on top of astrology — it's the same math, just expressed as a percentage.
guide.strengthBody: Your Day Master is the Heavenly Stem of your Day Pillar — the character that represents "you" specifically, separate from your overall dominant element. Ohaeng checks how much support that character gets from the rest of your chart: if at least half the other characters share or generate its element, you're a "strong" Day Master; otherwise, you're "weak." Strong doesn't mean better and weak doesn't mean worse — it's a read on whether your core traits show up consistently everywhere you go (strong) or shift more with who's around you (weak). You'll see this reflected on every avatar in the app too: a solid ring means a strong Day Master, a dashed ring means a weak one.
guide.featuresBody: Idol Match and Drama Match both work the same way: enter your birthday and gender, and Ohaeng scans the full roster — every idol group, or all 100 K-drama actors — filtered to the opposite gender, and surfaces whoever scores highest against your chart. Group Match works a little differently: pick one group, and instead of a single best match, you get every member ranked by score, so you can see exactly where your bias lands next to the rest of the lineup.
